title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is part of Grothendieck's group-scheme bookkeeping for the 'équation des lacets'. I read rho and sigma as the standard order-3 and order-2 generators of the modular group, as in the Longue Marche; this reading is inferred from context, not stated on the page.
- G is a GL_2-like group with special subgroup SG, determinant delta_G = det and projective quotient PG.
- T_rho is a torus (the centraliser of rho); N'_sigma is a normaliser-type group attached to sigma, with component character epsilon_sigma : N'_sigma -> mu_2 (or Z/2).
- On the previous page, M_{rho,sigma} is defined as the quotient of the product SG x S'T_rho x SN'_sigma x G_m by a diagonally embedded mu_2. Here S'T_rho = Ker(delta_rho^2) and SN'_sigma = Ker(delta'_sigma).
- A homomorphism out of this central product is therefore given by four homomorphisms on the factors, composed with the canonical maps J_G, J_rho, J_sigma, J_mu. These must have commuting images, and their product must be trivial on the diagonal mu_2.
- Page 448 did this for Theta_G (formula 138).

This page does the same for the remaining fundamental maps of diagram (134).
- (139) Theta_rho : M -> T_rho. It is trivial on SG and SN'_sigma, is the inclusion on S'T_rho, and is i_rho on G_m.
- (140) Theta_sigma : M -> N'_sigma. It is trivial on SG and S'T_rho, is the inclusion on SN'_sigma, and is i_sigma on G_m.
- (141) epsilon_3 : M -> mu_2. It is trivial on SG, SN'_sigma and G_m, and equals delta_rho restricted to S'T_rho. That restriction lands in mu_2 because S'T_rho = Ker(delta_rho^2).
- In each case Grothendieck notes 'compatibilités triviales'. Since the diagonal mu_2 lies in ST_rho, ST_sigma and the centre, the compatibility conditions are immediate.

(142) He then defines three derived homomorphisms:
- epsilon_2 = epsilon_sigma o Theta_sigma : M -> mu_2 (a 'component' character);
- chi = det o Theta_G : M -> G_m (a determinant character);
- tilde Theta = can o Theta_G : M -> PG.

(143) The combined map (chi, epsilon_3, epsilon_2) : M -> G_m x mu_2 x mu_2 is an epimorphism.
- chi is surjective via the G_m factor; as an fppf sheaf map, squaring on G_m is epi.
- epsilon_3 is surjective via S'T_rho -> mu_2.
- epsilon_2 is surjective via the component group of N'_sigma.

Purpose. The next page uses these maps to define the kernels M^+, M^0, R, SR, etc. It then derives the product decompositions (147) and the prismatic diagrams of cocartesian squares. All of this is structural set-up for the group schemes attached to the pair (rho, sigma) in the 'loop equation' study.
errors: In (139) the source of Theta_rho J_rho is written S'T_sigma (as both the image and the transcription read it). From the definitions on p.448 it should be S'T_rho = Ker(delta_rho^2); this is probably a slip of the pen.

The target written as 'Z/2' in the transcription is very likely Grothendieck's handwritten mu_2, consistent with the next page. The two agree only up to the usual identification away from characteristic 2.

The epimorphism claim in (143) is only valid in the fppf (or fpqc) sense. chi restricted to the G_m factor is presumably t -> t^2, assuming Theta_G J_mu is the scalar embedding into GL_2. That is not surjective on points in general, though it is an epimorphism of group schemes. Grothendieck does not comment on this.

ideas.what: Defining homomorphisms out of a central product (a quotient of a product of group schemes by a diagonal mu_2) via their restrictions to the factors, subject to commutation and triviality on the diagonal kernel.
ideas.modern_name: universal property of central products / amalgamated quotients of group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory / SGA3-style group scheme formalism

ideas.what: Characters det o Theta_G, a component character epsilon_sigma o Theta_sigma, and the projective quotient map, assembled into an epimorphism onto G_m x mu_2 x mu_2 whose kernels give a lattice of subgroups (M^+, M^0, R, SR).
ideas.modern_name: character group / abelianization data of a disconnected reductive group scheme (normalizer of torus)
ideas.where_published: unpublished notes 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (cote 140-3)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine bookkeeping. It specifies homomorphisms on the factors of a central product, checks the trivial compatibilities, and defines characters assembling into an epimorphism. The surrounding project (group schemes attached to the modular generators for the loop equation) is unpublished and of some historical interest, but nothing on this page is a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The symbols rendered ']' followed by a letter are the involution maps J: read 'Theta_rho J_G', 'Theta_rho J_sigma', 'Theta_rho J_rho', 'Theta_rho J_mu', and similarly for Theta_sigma and epsilon_3. The rendering '𝔞' stands for the subscript G.
'S^1 T' should read S'T (S-prime T), as on the previous page.
The targets written 'Z/2' are probably mu_2 in Grothendieck's hand (compare p.450, formula 145).
The struck-out word in the first line of (139) appears to be a deleted 'trivial'-like word, replaced by the phrase 'Theta_rho J_sigma triviaux'.
The text at the bottom right reads 'épimorphisme'.
